Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 05-Jun-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SECOND SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - JUNE 2025  
  SUBJECT: ECE 1071/ECE_1071 - BASIC ELECTRONICS  
  (MAKE-UP)  
  Basic Electronics [ECE- 1071]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)                A Germanium diode has a saturation current of 1pA at 27°C. Determine (a) Diode bias voltage        (4)  
  when diode current is 3mA (b) Diode bias current when the temperature changes to 340°K, for the  
  same bias voltage. (c) Also determine the dynamic resistance of the diode at this new temperature.  
  Clearly show all calculation steps  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)                Determine the value of W/L in figure that places M1 at the edge of saturation. Also, calculate the     (3)  
  drain voltage change for a 1-mV change at the gate. Assume µn C ox = 100 µ A/V2 and VTH = 0.2V  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)                Explain the term Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV). How does it affect the selection of diodes in a full-     (3)  
  wave and bridge rectifier circuit?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2A)                A sinusoidal voltage with 20-0-20 V applied to secondary of the transformer used for full wave         (4)  
  rectification. If the load resistance is 1KΩ, determine:  
  (a) Peak value of load current  
  (b) Average load current  
  (c) RMS load current  
  (d) Average output voltage  
  (e) Rms output voltage  
  (f) Efficiency  
  (g) Ripple factor  
  (h) PIV  
  Page 1 of 3

Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)   Design a Zener regulator network with R S = 500Ω, VZ = 12V and Vi = 50V. Determine the minimum (3)  
  and maximum values of R L and load current so that Zener diode remains in ON state and safe,  
  given that IZK = 2 mA and PZM =500mW. Draw the circuit diagram for the same.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2C)   Determine CMRR in dB for an OPAMP, if we obtain an output voltage of 5 V for input voltages of         (3)  
  $$V1 = 0.5 mV and V2 = -0.5 mV applied to non-inverting and inverting terminals respectively, and$$  
  10mV if both inputs V1 and V2 are 0.5mV.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3A)   Draw the circuit diagram of Op-Amp inverting summing amplifier with V1 , V2 as the input voltages      (4)  
  and derive the expression for output voltage. Also design the circuit using two Op-Amp's to obtain,  
  Vout = 6V1 + 0.2V2 + 4V3 where V1 , V2 , and V3 are input voltages. Assume RF= 10KΩ.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)   a. Encode the data bits 1111 into 7 bit even parity Hamming code.                                      (3)  
  b. Identify the corrupted position in the transmitted code 1101111 based on (7,4) even parity  
  Hamming code.  
  c. Modify the corrupted position and decode the correct data.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)   Implement a full adder using minimum number of logic gates. Assume A,B and Cin are inputs              (3)  
  whereas Sum and Carry are outputs. Obtain the Boolean expression for sum and carry using the  
  truth table.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)   Obtain the minimal sum of product expressions based on the sum of minterms given below using K- (4)  
  map and implement it using NAND gate.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)   Design a 3 bit Ripple down counter using negative edge triggered T flipflops and draw the output       (3)  
  waveforms showing all the possible states of the counter.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4C)   Consider a serial input data 10100110 fed to a 4-bit shift register circuit from LSB. Determine the  (3)  
  output for SISO operation after 5th clock pulse and the number of clock pulses required to shift MSB  
  bit to the output. Also, draw the circuit diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
$$5A)   Given an FM signal V FM(t) = 20 cos [2Π108 t + 5sin(2Π25000t)], Calculate carrier frequency,           (4)$$  
  modulating frequency, frequency deviation and bandwidth using Carson's rule.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)   Draw the block diagram of basic communication System and explain the function of each block.           (3)  
  
  
  Page 2 of 3

Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5C)                   For binary data 11010, sketch the ASK, FSK and PSK signals.                                        (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
